name: Pittsburgh
operatingHours: The T (Red and Blue lines) runs ~5:00 AM–~12:30 AM on weekdays, with fewer trains and shorter hours at weekends; the Silver Line runs a limited, mostly weekday service. Trains every ~10–30 min. No overnight service.
fareInfo: PRT base fare $2.75 (2026), valid for 3 hours of unlimited rides on the T, buses and the Monongahela Incline. Pay with a ConnectCard, the PRT mobile ticketing app or exact cash. Day pass ~$7. The T is free between downtown stations and the North Shore (Allegheny, North Side). The 28X Airport Flyer bus costs the same $2.75.

sights.name: Duquesne Incline
sights.note: An 1877 cable car that hauls riders up Mount Washington; the upper station's deck has the classic view of the Point and the three rivers.
sights.hours: Daily 6:30 AM–12:30 AM; pay the fare in cash or with a ConnectCard

sights.name: Phipps Conservatory and Botanical Gardens
sights.note: A Victorian glasshouse in Schenley Park with themed rooms, seasonal flower shows and outdoor gardens.
sights.hours: 9:30 AM–5:00 PM daily, till 10:00 PM Fri

sights.name: PNC Park
sights.note: The Pirates' riverside ballpark, often rated the best in baseball, with the skyline and the Clemente Bridge beyond the outfield.
sights.hours: Pirates home games Apr–Sep; 90-minute ballpark tours on select days

sights.name: Strip District
sights.note: A half-mile of produce stalls, fish mongers, ethnic grocers and sports-merch stands along Penn Avenue; busiest and best on Saturday mornings.
sights.hours: Most shops ~8:00 AM–5:00 PM, some closed Sun

sights.name: Carnegie Museum of Natural History
sights.note: Famous for its Dinosaur Hall of real skeletons, plus gems and Egyptian galleries; it shares a building with the Carnegie Museum of Art.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–5:00 PM, till 8:00 PM Thu, closed Tue

sights.name: Senator John Heinz History Center
sights.note: Six floors of western Pennsylvania history in a former ice warehouse, including Mister Rogers' set and the Western PA Sports Museum.

sights.name: National Aviary
sights.note: America's national bird zoo, with walk-through habitats, penguins and flight shows on the edge of Allegheny Commons park.

sights.name: Mount Washington (Grandview Avenue)
sights.note: Free overlooks along Grandview Avenue give the best view of downtown, especially at dusk; reach them by either incline.

sights.name: Bicycle Heaven
sights.note: A sprawling, free-spirited bicycle museum and shop with thousands of vintage bikes, from Pee-wee Herman's to rare Schwinns.

sights.name: Randyland
sights.note: Artist Randy Gilson's riot-of-colour house and courtyard in the Mexican War Streets, painted with murals and found objects.

sights.name: Pittsburgh Zoo & Aquarium
sights.note: A hillside zoo in Highland Park with elephants, big cats and a large aquarium wing.
sights.hours: ~9:30 AM–5:30 PM (last entry 4:30 PM); shorter winter hours

sights.name: The Andy Warhol Museum
sights.note: Seven floors devoted to Pittsburgh-born Andy Warhol, the largest single-artist museum in North America.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–5:00 PM, till 8:00 PM Fri, closed Tue

sights.name: Cathedral of Learning
sights.note: The University of Pittsburgh's 42-storey Gothic tower, with a vaulted ground-floor hall and 31 Nationality Rooms decorated by local ethnic communities.
sights.hours: Building open daily; Nationality Rooms visitable when not in use for classes, ~9:00 AM–4:00 PM

sights.name: Kamin Science Center
sights.note: A hands-on science museum by the Ohio River with a planetarium, a giant model railroad and a WWII submarine moored outside.

sights.name: Monongahela Incline
sights.note: The oldest working funicular in the US (1870), climbing from across the street from Station Square T stop to Grandview Avenue.
sights.hours: ~5:30 AM–12:45 AM Mon–Sat, ~8:45 AM–midnight Sun; standard PRT fare

sights.name: Point State Park
sights.note: The green tip of downtown where the rivers meet, with a big fountain, riverside lawns and the Fort Pitt Museum.

sights.name: Market Square
sights.note: Downtown's lively central plaza, ringed by restaurants and bars, with seasonal farmers' markets and a winter ice rink nearby.

sights.name: Roberto Clemente Bridge
sights.note: A golden 1928 suspension bridge between downtown and PNC Park, closed to cars and packed with fans on game days.

railStations.name: Pittsburgh Union Station
railStations.note: Amtrak station under the old Pennsylvania Railroad rotunda. The daily Pennsylvanian goes to Harrisburg, Philadelphia and New York (~9 h), and the long-distance Floridian runs to Chicago and to Washington and Miami. Steel Plaza T station is a ~7-minute walk.
railStations.hours: Waiting room open around the clock for the overnight Floridian; few trains a day, check timetables.

airports.name: Pittsburgh International Airport
airports.transitNote: The T doesn't go to the airport. PRT's 28X Airport Flyer bus (not on this map; $2.75) leaves from the new terminal's ground-transport level and runs to downtown in ~40 min, then to Oakland, every 30–40 min. A taxi or rideshare to downtown takes ~25–30 min.
